One validator was silently killing five sibling hooks

PR #3201 · fix/ungate-telemetry-from-output-validator · toggle the fix below to see what changes

SYNC_HOOKS, on the payload Claude Code actually sends

The dispatcher runs six hooks in order and returns immediately if any of them yields continue: false. Flip the toggle to see the difference this PR makes.

Every real SubagentStop event stops at hook 0. Five hooks behind it have never executed, including retry-handler, which is functional logic and not telemetry.

Root cause, proven at file and line

output-validator.ts:23     output = input.agent_output || input.output || ''
output-validator.ts:29-31  if (!output) errors.push('Agent produced empty output')
output-validator.ts:60     validationStatus = errors.length > 0 ? 'failed' : 'passed'
output-validator.ts:101-3  if (failed) return { continue: false }
                                              |
sync-subagent-stop-dispatcher.ts:67-69        v
                           if (result.continue === false) return result

unified-dispatcher.ts:349  "CC delivers neither duration_ms nor tool_input nor
                            agent_output/output at SubagentStop, 0 of 11,319
                            real rows carried any of them"   (#3034)
The chain closes deterministically. The field is absent on ~100% of real events, so the validator reports a failure on ~100% of real events, so the dispatcher returns at hook 0 on ~100% of real events. This is not flaky starvation. It is a kill switch.

A content-quality gate was wired to Claude Code's pipeline-stop semantics. It vetoed five unrelated hooks it was never designed to gate.

Distinguish "never sent" from "empty"

The validator could not tell a missing payload field from an agent that produced nothing. Those are different facts and only one of them is a defect.

- const output = input.agent_output || input.output || '';
+ const rawOutput      = input.agent_output ?? input.output;
+ const outputDelivered = typeof rawOutput === 'string';
+ const output          = rawOutput ?? '';

- if (!output) {
+ if (outputDelivered && !output) {
    validationErrors.push('Agent produced empty output');
  }

- if (outputLength < 50) {
+ if (outputDelivered && outputLength < 50) {
    validationWarnings.push(`Output seems very short (${outputLength} chars)`);
  }

Two fixes that were rejected, and why

approachverdictreason
Reorder SYNC_HOOKS so telemetry runs firstrejectedHides a broken validator instead of fixing it. The next hook added early reintroduces the bug.
Change the failed branch to continue: truerejectedDiscards block semantics where they are legitimate. An agent that genuinely returns nothing should still block.
Gate the checks on whether the field was deliveredshippedFixes the actual confusion. An explicitly delivered empty string still blocks, with a test pinning that.
The gate is not disabled. agent_output: '' still produces continue: false, and a test asserts it, so this cannot later be "simplified" into a no-op.

Why a 100%-reproducible bug survived two months of green CI

Every hook had a passing unit test

skill-channel-tracker.test.ts imports the handler and calls it directly. It never touches syncSubagentStopDispatcher. So it tested a scenario that does not occur in production, and passed, while the hook it covers had never run once.

There was no test for the dispatcher at all. This PR adds the first one.

The transferable lesson. A verification that shares the code's own assumption is not independent. An earlier adversarial pass on this same bug built a repro that supplied a non-empty agent_output, a value Claude Code never sends, and concluded the pipeline worked. The test went green; production wrote nothing.

The invariant the new suite pins

The dispatcher's ONLY early return is the continue===false short-circuit.
Therefore, on the real CC payload:

    result.continue !== false   ⟹   every hook in SYNC_HOOKS was reached

That is structural, not incidental, so it keeps holding as hooks are added.

Two tests corrected

  • One asserted continue === false for an absent field. That assertion was the bug written down as a contract.
  • One claimed to cover a null-ish field but passed undefined into a defaulted parameter, so JS default substitution made it a duplicate of the empty-string case. It verified nothing.
